summary: A light-to-medium abstract tile-drafting game where players take colored tiles from shared factory displays to build patterns on their own board, scoring for adjacency and completed rows while being careful not to get stuck with leftover penalty tiles. It's quick to teach, tense in a quiet way, and looks beautiful on the table.
praised: simple rules with surprisingly sharp tactical depth
criticised: can feel a bit solitaire-ish since boards develop independently

interaction.detail: Players draft from shared factory displays and can deliberately take tiles they don't need just to dump penalty tiles on an opponent, but each player builds their pattern on their own private board. The shared supply of tiles is the main point of contact between players.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Scoring comes from just two things: adjacency chains scored as you tile your wall each round, and the end-game completion bonuses for rows, columns, and colors.
scoring.how_you_win: Draft tiles to complete pattern rows so they score adjacency points on your wall, avoid floor-line penalties, and pick up end-game bonuses for finished rows/columns/colors.
